docs.overview_title: The import journey at a glance
docs.overview_lead: Every import follows the same six steps. The sections below explain the rules, systems, documents and costs behind each one.

flow.caption: From finding a product to receiving it: the six steps of an import into Israel.

personal.caption: Personal imports by declared value (USD). Rates and limits change; confirm on gov.il before ordering.

weight.caption: Airlines charge for space as well as weight: you pay for whichever is larger.
weight.box_label: A carton with length, width and height marked
weight.example: Example: 60 × 40 × 50 cm ÷ 6000 = 20 kg volumetric. Actual 14 kg → you pay for 20 kg.

cascade.caption: Each tax is calculated on top of the layer before it, so a higher Customs Duty also raises Purchase Tax and VAT.

chart.title: Where the money goes: a sample import
chart.caption: Sample: $10,000 goods + $1,200 freight (USD = ₪3.70), 0.35% insurance premium, 12% Customs Duty, 15% Purchase Tax, ₪2,300 local expenses, 18% VAT. Calculated with this site's calculator.

docs.documents_caption: Certificates of origin you may need. Open one to view it full size.

1.callout: Limits and VAT rates change (VAT has been 18% since 2025). Check the Tax Authority under <websites>Websites</websites> before you order.

2.callout: Vehicle imports have strict standards and paperwork. Talk to a licensed customs broker before you buy.

3.callout: Find your product's HS code in Shaar Olami, then use its Customs Duty and Purchase Tax rates in the <calc>calculator</calc>.

4.callout: Apply for licenses and approvals before the goods ship. Goods waiting at the port for approval pay storage fees.

5.callout: A valid certificate of origin can cut or cancel the Customs Duty under a trade agreement. See the samples above.

6.callout: Counterfeit and prohibited goods are seized at customs and can lead to fines. When in doubt, ask before you order.

7.callout: Use the <air>Air Shipment calculator</air>: it works out the chargeable weight for every carton for you.

8.callout: Wood packaging without the ISPM 15 stamp can be rejected or destroyed at the port, at your cost.

9.callout: Rules differ from regular imports. Confirm the procedure with a customs broker before you ship.

10.callout: Run your own numbers in the <calc>calculator</calc>. Trade terms like CIF and FOB are explained under <terms>Terms</terms>.

customs_duty.title: Customs Duty rate
customs_duty.body: The duty rate set in the Israeli Customs Tariff for your product's tariff item (HS code). It is charged as a percentage of the CIF value (Cost + Freight + Insurance).
customs_duty.example:
CIF value: ₪10,000
Customs Duty rate: 12%
Customs Duty = 10,000 × 12% = ₪1,200
customs_duty.tip: Find the rate for your HS code on the Israel Customs Tariff website (Shaar Olami). Many goods have 0%.

duty_option_i.title: Duty Option I
duty_option_i.body: Some tariff items have a compound duty: two ways to calculate it, and the law takes the higher one (ALF – not less than) or the lower one (ALE – not more than). Option I is usually the percentage-based duty, entered as an amount in ₪.
duty_option_i.example:
CIF value: ₪10,000
Tariff: 12% or ₪3 per pair
Option I = 10,000 × 12% = ₪1,200 → enter 1200
duty_option_i.tip: You can type the calculation directly, e.g. 10000*12/100.

duty_option_ii.title: Duty Option II
duty_option_ii.body: The second way to calculate a compound duty, usually a fixed amount per unit (kg, pair, litre, item), entered as an amount in ₪. Choose "Higher of two" or "Lower of two" above to match the tariff wording.
duty_option_ii.example:
500 pairs × ₪3 per pair = ₪1,500 → enter 1500
Higher of two (ALF): Customs Duty = ₪1,500
Lower of two (ALE): Customs Duty = ₪1,200
duty_option_ii.tip: You can type the calculation directly, e.g. 500*3.
